title: Reliable SEED and LIVE provider recovery
problem: When a provider has no usable nodes, Mihomo can treat its default COMPATIBLE fallback as direct and stop before the configured recovery route. Users then cannot reliably start from SEED or recover a missing LIVE provider.
outcome: Generated profiles keep the public PROVIDER-AUTO name and source node names, select healthy LIVE nodes when available, fall back to SEED when LIVE is empty or unavailable, and fetch LIVE in the order PRIVATE, SEED, then DIRECT while retaining usable cached LIVE nodes after failed updates.

actors.name: Profile user
actors.responsibility: Receive a valid profile and working proxy route during normal operation and recovery.

actors.name: Service operator
actors.responsibility: Publish recoverable provider profiles and verify the deployed runtime behavior.

in_scope: Preserve the public PROVIDER-AUTO group name and healthy LIVE preference.
Keep source node names unchanged and exclude LIVE, SEED, and BOOTSTRAP prefixes.
Keep physical provider nodes out of the explicit GLOBAL policy group.
Render an optional validated mihomo.hosts map from protected runtime config only.
Make empty PRIVATE and LIVE groups unavailable to fallback selection so the declared SEED recovery paths can run.
Preserve the PRIVATE to SEED to DIRECT provider fetch order and the existing LIVE cache on failed updates.
Correct the test-client dependency that causes the Starlette deprecation warning and verify the patch through tests, build, Mihomo, and deployment checks.
out_of_scope: Changing Cloudflare configuration or security policy without separate authorization.
Renaming public groups or redesigning the existing SEED/LIVE provider architecture.

invariants.claim: The public provider group remains named PROVIDER-AUTO.
invariants.enforcement: Profile rendering assertions and the published profile inspection verify the exact group name.

invariants.claim: An empty PRIVATE selector or LIVE selector cannot become an implicit COMPATIBLE route that short-circuits recovery.
invariants.enforcement: Generated resilient profiles set empty-fallback to REJECT on PRIVATE and PROVIDER-AUTO-LIVE; regression tests and real Mihomo probes verify that selection advances to SEED.

invariants.claim: Provider downloads try PRIVATE, then SEED, then DIRECT without recursion.
invariants.enforcement: Generated group ordering is asserted and isolated runtime tests exercise the route.

invariants.claim: A failed LIVE update does not remove a previously usable LIVE cache.
invariants.enforcement: Provider service tests and isolated runtime verification check cache retention after an update error.

invariants.claim: No Cloudflare configuration is changed as part of this recovery patch.
invariants.enforcement: Deployment and troubleshooting remain limited to the authorized application and origin paths.

invariants.claim: The group-scoped inline SEED provider is available to normal and fetch groups without a duplicate top-level proxy list.
invariants.enforcement: Renderer assertions verify group-scoped provider references and no top-level proxies; an isolated Mihomo cold-start verifies the LIVE download route can use SEED.

invariants.claim: An optional exact hostname-to-IP map is read only from protected Mihomo runtime config and cannot be changed through UI settings.
invariants.enforcement: Config tests validate exact hostnames and unscoped IP addresses, settings-overlay tests reject mihomo.hosts, and public/gateway profile tests verify rendering.

failure_model.failure: LIVE is absent, empty, or unhealthy during startup.
failure_model.response: Reject the empty LIVE group and select the usable SEED group.
Reject the empty PRIVATE group so fallback can proceed to SEED and then DIRECT.

failure_model.failure: An HTTP provider starts before the inline SEED provider is initialized.
failure_model.response: Use the inline SEED provider through its hidden url-test group in the fetch route while retaining that same provider for normal runtime group selection.

failure_model.failure: A LIVE provider refresh fails after a valid cache exists.
failure_model.response: Retain the existing cached LIVE provider and keep it available for later selection.

failure_model.failure: The public edge returns response headers but does not deliver a body.
failure_model.response: Record the feed and client checks as unverified and leave Cloudflare settings untouched absent separate authorization.

acceptance_signals: The complete backend suite passes without the Starlette TestClient warning in the development environment.
The frontend build, generated profile checks, and Mihomo validation pass.
Runtime probes show LIVE when healthy, SEED when LIVE is empty or unhealthy, and the PRIVATE to SEED to DIRECT fetch order.
A failed LIVE refresh preserves the previous usable cache.
The pushed and deployed commit is verified by SHA, and published-feed and local-client results are recorded from actual responses and traffic.
